    for i in range(1, m + 1):
        for j in range(1, n + 1):
            if str1[i - 1] == str2[j - 1]:
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1] + 1
            else:
                dp[i][j] = max(dp[i - 1][j], dp[i][j - 1])
    
    # Following the dp table to get the longest common subsequence.
    index = dp[m][n]
    lcs = [""] * (index + 1)

            j -= 1
            index -= 1
        elif dp[i - 1][j] > dp[i][j - 1]:

2. **Recursive Case**: In this part of the function, the function calls itself with a simpler version of the original problem, moving closer to the base case with each call. This process continues until the base case is reached.

    # Recursive case

        return n * factorial(n-1)

Understanding and optimizing the computational complexity of algorithms is crucial for developing efficient software, especially when dealing with large datasets or real-time systems.

continuation: React.js updates the user interface through a process called the Virtual DOM. When state or props change in a React component, instead of directly updating the real DOM, React first creates a virtual representation of the DOM (Virtual DOM).
